answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each identity to a continuously refreshed Wesolowski VDF: identity verification requires a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each square depending on the previous result. An attacker may assign clones to GPUs, but cannot split one chain into parallel work or shortcut its delay; every additional identity incurs another physical sequential-time cost. A violet bridge and a sonnet can label epochs, but neither changes the cryptographic bottleneck
